environment.description: Same Ktor service deployed behind AWS AppSync with a custom authorizer Lambda that validates tenant claims from Cognito JWT before establishing the GraphQL subscription (which proxies to the WebSocket). The PostgreSQL RDS instance has an additional SECURITY DEFINER function `set_tenant_context()` that is the ONLY way to set app.current_tenant - it cross-references the pg_catalog session variable `rds.restrict_session_variables` (set to 'on' at the parameter group level) which prevents direct SET commands on app.* namespace from non-superuser roles. The app_user role has EXECUTE permission only on set_tenant_context(jwt_sub text) which internally validates the tenant mapping via a tenants_users junction table before setting the session variable. Additionally, the RDS instance has a pg_audit extension logging all SET commands, and a CloudWatch alarm triggers on any direct SET app.current_tenant that bypasses the function.

config.rds_parameter_group: rds.restrict_session_variables = on, preventing app_user from executing SET app.current_tenant directly
config.db_function: SECURITY DEFINER set_tenant_context(jwt_sub) validates tenant membership before setting variable
config.app_user_permissions: REVOKE ALL ON SCHEMA public FROM app_user; GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION set_tenant_context TO app_user; standard DML grants with RLS enforced
config.appsync_authorizer: Lambda validates Cognito JWT, extracts tenant_id from custom:tenant claim, rejects connections without valid token
config.network: Private ALB, AppSync endpoint is the only public ingress for WebSocket traffic
config.monitoring: pg_audit on SET commands, CloudWatch alarm on bypass attempts
